title: Oily water separator and the 15 ppm rule explained

scenes.label: KNOW YOUR EQUIPMENT
scenes.heading: 15 ppm. The limit every engineer must respect.
scenes.narration: 15 ppm. Pump bilge water overboard above that limit, and you have broken MARPOL.

scenes.label: WHAT IT DOES
scenes.heading: The oily water separator
scenes.body: It removes oil from machinery space bilge water so that only water within the legal limit goes overboard.
scenes.narration: The oily water separator cleans machinery space bilge water, so that only water within the legal limit goes overboard.

scenes.label: MARPOL ANNEX I
scenes.heading: Discharge is allowed only when

items.title: Approved oil filtering equipment is used
Oil content is 15 ppm or less
Alarm and automatic stop work
items.text: Required in special areas and from 10,000 GT

scenes.narration: MARPOL Annex 1 allows the discharge only when the ship is en route, the water passes through approved oil filtering equipment, and the oil content is not more than 15 ppm without dilution. Where fitted, the alarm and automatic stopping device must work.

scenes.label: COMMON MISTAKE
scenes.heading: The Oil Record Book does not match
scenes.body: Record every bilge operation in Oil Record Book Part I without delay. Inspectors compare entries with tank soundings.
scenes.narration: Record every bilge operation in the Oil Record Book Part 1 without delay. Port State Control will compare your entries with the tank soundings.

scenes.label: KEY TAKEAWAY
scenes.heading: Never bypass the separator.
scenes.narration: And never, under any circumstances, bypass the separator.

sources.title: International Convention for the Prevention of Pollution from Ships (MARPOL), Annex I
